prompt: Which order lines were sent more than once? This table may hold errors. Two lines are copies of one order line when order_id, product_id, quantity, unit_price_eur, promo_id and line_discount_eur all match, with a missing promo_id matching a missing one. Return three columns, in this order: order_id, product_id and n_lines, the number of matching lines. Return one row for each set of two or more matching lines. Any row order is fine.

output_contract.grain: one row per order line sent more than once

hints: Next, write the group filter that keeps the sets with more than one line.
Each group is one set of matching lines; HAVING tests its size after the lines are counted.
faded_shape:
SELECT order_id, product_id, COUNT(*) AS n_lines
FROM order_lines
GROUP BY order_id, product_id, quantity, unit_price_eur, promo_id, line_discount_eur
why_this_works: Grouping by every column but order_line_id puts a copy and its original in one group, and HAVING keeps the groups with more than one line.
